item.title: The first homology of square-section braid groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.12633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the first homology of the unordered configuration space of $n$ open unit-squares in the $w$ by $h$ rectangle for all positive integers $n$, $w$, and $h$. Letting $w$ and $h$ vary, these square configuration spaces form a bi-filtration of the unordered configuration space of $n$ points in the plane, so their fundamental groups approximate the $n$-strand braid group. Using a pair of spectral sequences, we prove that these square and point configuration spaces have naturally isomorphic first homology groups if $w,h\ge 3$ and $n\le wh-3$. In the $h=2$ case, we show that the first homology groups of these square configuration spaces are free of rank $n-1$ for $n\le 2w-2$, whereas they are free of rank $w-1$ for $n=2w-1$.
item.dc:creator: Minh Pham, Nicholas Wawrykow, Jacob Zweiback

item.title: Derived plethystic algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.12839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove comparison results about $\infty$-categories of derived commutative rings with extra algebraic structure. For example, we show that several notions of derived $\delta$-rings agree and obtain similar results for derived $\lambda$-rings, derived binomial rings, and derived Boolean rings. Our comparison results apply more generally to modules over a specific kind of monad on derived rings that we call derived plethory.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Antieau, Edith H\"ubner, Dmitry Kubrak, Joost Nuiten

item.title: Critical Point Theory for the Distance Function on PL-Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the (typical) singularities of the distance function from a point in the ambient space to a polytopal complex in Euclidean space. By means of the Goresky-MacPherson splitting we generalize the existing linear theory to the quadratic distance function. Critical points occur on `selected' strata of the PL-space, where normal Morse Data determine the change of topology. On the homology level there exist indices with multiplicities, combined in a Morse vector. We focus mainly on PL-manifolds. We give bounds, depending on the dimension of the strata. In low dimensions we describe singularity types. At the end we discuss relations with Discrete Morse Theory.
item.dc:creator: Dirk Siersma

item.title: Reconstruction of graphs and surfaces from derived categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.13488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A pair of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$ is a \emph{Fourier--Mukai (FM) pair} if there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories of derived sheaves of abelian groups \[\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))\simeq \operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z)).\] An FM pair $(X,Y)$ is \emph{non-trivial} if $X$ and $Y$ are not homeomorphic. We consider the question of whether non-trivial FM pairs $(X,Y)$ exist for which $X$ and $Y$ are both "nice" spaces, which in this article means admitting a triangulation. We show that the answer is no if $X$ is second-countable and either (i) one-dimensional, (ii) a surface, or (iii) the 3-sphere. In order to prove this, we define two invariants of dualizable categories. The first invariant is an extension of \emph{Tate--Hochschild cohomology} (aka singular Hochschild cohomology) to a class of dualizable categories satisfying a countability assumption. For a homology manifold $X$, we relate the Tate--Hochschild cohomology of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))$ to the homology at infinity of $X$ (in the sense of proper homotopy theory). The second invariant takes the form of a subcategory $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{Gor}}\subseteq\mathcal D$ called the \emph{Gorenstein locus}, defined for every dualizable stable category $\mathcal D$. For a triangularizable space $X$ and a field $k$, we show that the Gorenstein locus of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(k))$ is equal to the full subcategory of sheaves supported on the $k$-homology manifold locus of $X$.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Harr

item.title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.13803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models. We use it to prove that two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms are homotopic \`a la Seidel if and only if, considered as morphisms of 2-colored DG operads, they are elementary homotopic \`a la Markl-Shnider-Stasheff through a homotopy which is constant on the two monochromatic parts. We also provide an example of two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms which are elementary homotopic but not weakly equivalent (and so homotopic \`a la Seidel). Moreover, over a field, we observe that the models for the interval are good path objects in the category of A$_{\infty}$-algebras with (non strict) A$_{\infty}$-morphisms, and we explain why weakly equivalent A$_{\infty}$-morphisms need not be homotopic.
item.dc:creator: Mattia Ornaghi

item.title: Weak and genuine A_n-formality for number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.11390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce weak $A_n$-formality for Galois cochain algebras and, for profinite groups whose mod-$p$ cohomology is concentrated in degrees at most two, characterise weak and genuine $A_n$-formality through finite embedding problems and the projective system they form. We then study $A_n$-formality for number fields. Let $K$ be a number field and let $p$ be an odd prime with $\mu_p\not\subset K$. For $p\geq 5$, and for $p=3$ under a natural local cyclotomic condition, we prove that every associated finite $A_3$-embedding problem is solvable. In contrast, for every odd $p$ with $\mu_p\not\subset K$, we show that no compatible family of finite-stage solutions exists, and hence $C^\bullet(G_K,\mathbb F_p)$ is not genuinely $A_3$-formal. The proof uses Chebotarev density, governing fields, and the Gras-Munnier criterion to obstruct the compatibility of finite-stage solutions, and it builds on previous work of Maire-Min\'a\v{c}-Ramakrishna-T\^an. This shows that genuine $A_3$-formality detects a global compatibility obstruction for number fields invisible to every individual finite embedding problem and invisible to obstructions arising from individual strong Massey vanishing problems.
item.dc:creator: Ambrus P\'al, Gereon Quick

item.title: Semi-topological Galois cohomology and Weierstrass realizability
item.description: arXiv:2412.08469v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Semi-topological Galois theory associates a canonical finite splitting covering to a monic Weierstrass polynomial. The inverse limit of the corresponding deck groups defines the absolute semi-topological Galois group, $\PiST(X,x)$. This paper develops a cohomology theory for $\PiST(X,x)$ with discrete torsion coefficients, establishing its fundamental properties and canonical comparison maps to singular cohomology. A Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence is used to yield an obstruction theory for semi-topological embedding problems. We prove several structural and vanishing results, including ST-fullness for free fundamental groups and triviality for finite fundamental groups. As applications, we provide a criterion for lifting finite projective monodromy to linear monodromy, formulate the $\pi_1$-detectable Weierstrass realizability conjecture for divisor classes and show that this conjecture is true for abelian varieties, smooth complex projective curves and ruled surfaces over positive-genus curves.
item.dc:creator: Jyh-Haur Teh

item.title: Galois actions on surfaces and a higher genus Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group
item.description: arXiv:2606.01466v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a modular operad $\mathbf{S}$ of mapping class groupoids modelling the higher-genus Teichm\"uller tower, with compositions and contractions encoding surface gluing. We prove a presentation theorem for maps out of $\mathbf{S}$ using genus-zero and genus-one generators and relations. Applying the work of Nakamura--Schneps, we obtain a faithful action of their subgroup $\widehat{\Gamma}\subseteq \widehat{\mathsf{GT}}$ on $\widehat{\mathbf{S}}$, and hence a faithful Galois action. The genus-zero truncation identifies with the cyclic operad of parenthesized ribbon braids, whose object-fixing profinite automorphism group is $\widehat{\mathsf{GT}}$. The completed classifying spaces form a modular $\infty$-operad whose corolla values are geometric \'etale homotopy types of moduli stacks of curves with nonzero tangent vectors at their marked points. The $\widehat{\Gamma}$-action induces a faithful action by homotopy automorphisms on the associated tower of profinite homotopy $1$-types, which agrees with the \'etale model in genus zero and one.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Basualdo Bonatto, Marcy Robertson

item.title: On the automorphism groups of smooth Fano threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2406.03584v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a smooth Fano threefold over the complex numbers of Picard rank $1$ with finite automorphism group. We give numerical restrictions on the order of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{X})$ provided the genus $g(\mathcal{X})\leq 10$ and $\mathcal{X}$ is not an ordinary smooth Gushel-Mukai threefold. More precisely, we show that the order $|\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{X})|$ divides a certain explicit number depending on the genus of $\mathcal{X}$. We use a classification of Fano threefolds in terms of complete intersections in homogeneous varieties and the previous paper of A. Gorinov and the author regarding the topology of spaces of regular sections.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Konovalov

item.title: Path homology of circulant digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2602.04140v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study GLMY path homology of circulant digraphs through step-word complexes and infinite cyclic lifts. We first prove chain retractions for interval connection sets. For a fixed finite positive connection set $S$ containing $1$, the infinite lift yields a split exact sequence and all-degree stability over every field. We then encode the short additive relations of $S$ in a lattice lift and obtain exterior homology in arbitrarily high degrees for collision-free step sets. Under an exact Freiman admissibility condition, we classify all connection sets with three positive steps. For arbitrarily many steps, we compute rectangular additive configurations and arithmetic progressions over every field, and doubling strings in characteristic zero, including their boundary ranks.
item.dc:creator: Xinxing Tang, Shing-Tung Yau

item.title: Motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells and the connective formal group law
item.description: arXiv:2605.26556v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use the connective formal group law to define a one-parameter ($\beta$-)deformation of the motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells in the $d$-step flag variety. This $\beta$-deformation specializes to the motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells when $\beta=1$ and to the Segre-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of Schubert cells when $\beta=0$ (though the $\beta$-deformations are not simply the $\beta$-homogenizations of the motivic Segre classes). We define rational function representatives for the $\beta$-deformed classes in the $d=1$ case in terms of a solvable lattice model, and we prove a combinatorial formula for the structure constants in the $\beta$-deformed basis in the $d=1$ case using Knutson-Tao puzzles. Unexpectedly, the structure constants are built out of entries of $R$-matrices for the multi-parameter quantum group of type $\widehat{a}_2$ (which suggests an action of multi-parameter quantum groups on equivariant connective $K$-rings of Nakajima quiver varieties, with their convolution algebra structures). We show that our $\beta$-deformations arise from canonical elements in a quotient of the torus-equivariant algebraic cobordism ring of the cotangent bundle of the flag variety by proving that the canonical elements satisfy a GKM type condition (in future work, we will show that these canonical elements also lie in the torus-equivariant connective $K$-ring, in the sense of Karpenko--Merkurjev, of this cotangent bundle).
item.dc:creator: Raj Gandhi

item.title: Learning Transfers: Kan Extensions of Topological Invariants of Learned Representations
item.description: arXiv:2606.07627v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When a learned representation is reused for a new task, which of its structure should survive? A task is a small category, a change of task is a functor $J$, and the invariants of a trained representation form a functor $F$. The left Kan extension $\operatorname{Lan}_JF$ is the invariant that the source and the change of task force on the target: by its universal property, every comparison of the source with an observed target invariant factors through it. The transfer discrepancy is the largest distance, over the target objects, between this extension and the observed invariant. For persistent homology the extension is a cokernel over comma categories, and a functorial version of the discrepancy, which also compares the maps between target objects, is $1$-Lipschitz under interleavings. On finite samples the discrepancy is a bottleneck distance, computed without approximation. For data glued from two pieces whose exclusive parts lie farther apart than the filtration scale, a Mayer-Vietoris sequence identifies what extending homology loses, while extending chains loses nothing. For a merge of labelled point clouds, the degree-zero discrepancy vanishes if and only if some $1$-Lipschitz classifier has a margin above the filtration scale at every sample point. In experiments on sampled manifolds, trained encoders and pretrained image models, every exact prediction holds on every sample. The discrepancy of truncated invariants recovers a hidden merge of separated parts far above chance and tells the intended target of a merge from a permuted control, but across pretrained models it does not track the accuracy of a linear probe.
item.dc:creator: Luciano Melodia
